Every meeting generates decisions, context, and commitments that your team needs to act on — but when the call ends, those details start fading fast. Scattered notes, missed action items, and hours lost re-reading unclear summaries are a daily frustration for teams of every size. Learning how to transcribe a meeting solves that problem by converting spoken conversation into a searchable, structured written record that your whole team can reference, share, and build on. This guide walks through every method — from manual workflows to fully automated AI transcription — and explains how to choose the right approach for your team.

## What is meeting transcription?


Meeting transcription is the process of converting the spoken audio from a meeting into written text. A useful transcript goes beyond raw speech-to-text: it includes speaker attribution (who said what), timestamps, and enough context that a reader can reconstruct the conversation without having been in the room. If you've ever wondered how[AI note-taking tools save time and keep teams focused](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/ai-note-taker-save-time-stay-focused/) , transcription is the foundation — the raw material that makes summaries, action items, and searchable meeting records possible.


Modern AI tools pair transcription with automated summaries and action item extraction, so you don't walk away with a wall of text — you walk away with a document that's actually usable.


## Manual vs. AI meeting transcription


Before deciding how to transcribe your next meeting, it helps to understand what your options are.


Method How it works Best for Key limitations


Manual transcription A person types out what's said during or after the meeting High-stakes legal or compliance recordings Slow, expensive, requires a dedicated notetaker


AI transcription Software automatically converts speech to text in real time Most business meetings Accuracy can vary with heavy accents or specialized jargon


Hybrid approach AI captures the transcript; a human reviews and edits Teams that need both speed and precision Requires some post-meeting review time


For most small and midsize business (SMB) teams, AI transcription is the practical choice. It's faster, more consistent, and increasingly accurate across a wide range of speaking styles — and it frees everyone in the meeting to actually participate, rather than type.


## How to transcribe a meeting: step by step


Whether you're using a dedicated tool or a built-in platform feature, the core workflow follows the same general arc.


**Step 1: Choose your transcription method**


Decide whether you'll transcribe live during the meeting or from a recording afterward. Live AI transcription tends to be more actionable — you can follow along in real time, flag key moments as they happen, and end the meeting with a transcript already ready.


**Step 2: Enable transcription before the meeting starts**


If you're using a tool like My Notes in Zoom Workplace, confirm that transcription is enabled in your account settings. For in-person meetings, open your mobile app and start note-taking before the conversation begins so nothing is missed.


**Step 3: Let participants know they're being transcribed**


Inform everyone in the meeting that the conversation is being captured. This is both a professional courtesy and, depending on your location, a legal requirement. Many tools display an active indicator during transcription, but a quick verbal heads-up is good practice regardless.


**Step 4: Stay in the conversation — let the tool work**


Once transcription is running, keep your attention on the discussion. Most AI note-taking tools handle speaker labels, timestamps, and full dialogue capture automatically. Use the live transcript to highlight decisions or action items as they come up, which makes the post-meeting review much faster.


**Step 5: Review and clean up**


After the meeting, skim the transcript for any misheard technical terms, unclear speaker labels, or filler words you'd like to remove. Good AI tools make inline editing quick. This step typically takes a few minutes, not a full re-read.


**Step 6: Extract action items and share**


Turn the transcript into a structured summary with clear action items, owners, and due dates. AI tools can do much of this automatically. Then share the notes with attendees — or anyone who missed the meeting.


## Types of meetings you can transcribe


Transcription isn't limited to video calls. Here's where it applies:


- **Virtual meetings.** Calls on Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet are the most common use case. AI tools that integrate natively with these platforms can start capturing the moment a meeting begins — no manual setup required.
- **In-person meetings.** Mobile note-taking apps can transcribe room conversations using your phone's microphone, making it practical to document in-person standups, client visits, and workshops without a laptop.
- **Hybrid meetings.** When some participants are remote and others are in the room, transcription tools that handle mixed audio sources are key to capturing a complete record.
- **Phone calls and walkthroughs.** Sales calls, client check-ins, and internal briefings can often be transcribed and summarized like any other meeting, giving your team a consistent archive.

## Security and privacy in meeting transcription


Before adopting any transcription tool, a few security considerations are worth working through as a team.


**Consent and notification.** Most jurisdictions require at least one party — and many require all parties — to consent to recording and transcription. Build consent notification into your meeting routine: a verbal heads-up or an in-app indicator covers the basics, but consult your legal or compliance team for industry-specific requirements.


**Where transcripts live.** Find out where your transcript data is stored, who can access it, and how long it's retained. With My Notes in Zoom Workplace, transcripts are private to the individual user by default and are not automatically shared with other meeting participants.


**Admin controls.** For teams handling sensitive conversations, look for tools that let administrators configure transcription permissions at the account, group, or user level. My Notes includes these controls so account owners and admins can set policies that match their organization's needs.


## Frequently asked questions about how to transcribe a meeting


### **What is the difference between a meeting transcript and meeting notes?**


A meeting transcript is a verbatim or near-verbatim written record of everything said during a meeting, typically with speaker labels and timestamps. Meeting notes are a curated summary of key decisions, action items, and important discussion points — shorter and more structured. AI tools like My Notes in Zoom Workplace can produce both: a full transcript for reference and an organized summary for everyday use, so you don't have to choose between completeness and clarity.


### **Can Zoom transcribe a meeting automatically?**


Yes. My Notes in Zoom Workplace can capture a live transcript during Zoom meetings with speaker attribution — no manual recording or separate tool required. With eligible paid plans, AI generates meeting summaries and next steps from the transcript automatically. My Notes can also capture notes from select third-party platforms — refer to Zoom's current documentation for details on supported platform coverage.


### **How do I transcribe an in-person meeting?**


For in-person conversations, you can use the mobile version of My Notes in Zoom Workplace. When your microphone is active on your mobile device, My Notes can capture and transcribe the conversation in the room. If you prefer, you can also record the audio on a separate device and upload it to a transcription tool after the meeting ends — though live transcription during the meeting is faster and typically more accurate.


### **Is it legal to transcribe a meeting?**


Recording and transcription laws vary by country and by state or province. In general, "one-party consent" laws allow recording as long as at least one participant (often the person doing the recording) has consented. Many jurisdictions require "all-party consent," meaning every participant must be notified. Check the laws applicable to your location and industry before transcribing meetings that involve external parties, clients, or employees in different regions.


### **What makes a good meeting transcript?**


A useful transcript goes beyond raw speech-to-text. It includes accurate speaker attribution, clear timestamps, and — ideally — an AI-generated summary with key decisions and action items highlighted. The goal is a document your team can search, share, and reference weeks later without re-listening to a recording. Structured notes with clear owners and due dates make follow-through far more likely than a raw text file alone.


### **What's the best way to transcribe a meeting on mobile?**


For mobile transcription during a Zoom meeting or an in-person conversation, My Notes in Zoom Workplace is built to work on mobile. Open the app, start your meeting or in-person session, and My Notes can begin capturing. Notes and transcripts sync to desktop automatically, so you can finish reviewing or sharing from your computer later without losing any context.
